339714.title: The generalized Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant conjecture for cyclic groups
339714.statement:
Let $C_n$ be the cyclic group of order $n$, and let $\mathsf s^{(k)}(C_n)$ denote its generalized Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant: the least integer $\ell$ such that every sequence of $\ell$ elements of $C_n$ contains a subsequence of length $kn$ whose sum is zero. **Generalized Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv conjecture.** For any integer $n$ and any integer $k$, 
$$
\mathsf s^{(k)}(C_n)=n+k.
$$
 The paper notes that the preceding proof uses the Cauchy–Davenport theorem only for prime moduli, while the corresponding statement for general $n$ is not established by that argument; the conjecture is presented as an expected extension to all cyclic groups.

340436.title: Rolek–Song's coloring conjecture for graphs with no $K_t$ minor
340436.statement:
Let $t\geq 1$, and let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices. A graph is **$(t-1)$-colorable** if its vertices can be properly colored with at most $t-1$ colors. **Rolek–Song's conjecture.** If $G$ has at least

$$
(t-2)n-\binom{t-1}{2}+1
$$

edges, then either $G$ has a $K_t$ minor or $G$ is $(t-1)$-colorable. The conjecture would extend the known relationship between extremal functions for clique minors and graph coloring to every $t\geq 1$; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
340436.exact_gap_or_derivation: No graph-universal coloring/minor mechanism. Complete graphs satisfy the minor alternative, and adding many edges may create the excluded minor. Need either a graph above the exact edge threshold with chromatic number >=t and no K_t minor, or a proof all such graphs contain that minor. Boundary t=1/empty graphs not credited.

336618.title: Kostochka–Mubayi–Verstraëte loose 5-cycle Ramsey conjecture
336618.statement:
For each $k\geq3$, let $LC_5^{(k)}$ be the $k$-uniform loose 5-cycle, and let $r_k(LC_5,n)$ denote its Ramsey number against a complete $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. **Kostochka–Mubayi–Verstraëte conjecture.** There is a constant $c=c_k>0$ such that

$$
r_k(LC_5,n)<c n^{5/4}.
$$

The source records a lower bound of order $(n/\log n)^{5/4}$ and presents this as the conjectured matching polynomial upper bound. The correct order remains open.
336618.exact_gap_or_derivation: Need independent-set size Omega(N^(4/5)) in every loose-C5-free k-uniform hypergraph, with k-dependent constant, to yield the stated upper bound. A lower-bound construction cannot establish this; no full structural/supersaturation argument.

333834.title: Bondy–Erdős conjecture for multicolour Ramsey numbers of odd cycles
333834.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$ and let $n>3$ be odd. Write $R_k(C_n)$ for the least integer $N$ such that every colouring of the edges of the complete graph $K_N$ with $k$ colours contains a monochromatic cycle $C_n$. **Bondy–Erdős conjecture.**

$$
R_k(C_n)=2^{k-1}(n-1)+1.
$$

This conjecture concerns the exact determination of multicolour Ramsey numbers for odd cycles, a class for which exact results were previously known mainly in the two-colour case. The paper addresses the conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
333834.exact_gap_or_derivation: Standard recursive two-part coloring supplies the lower bound: start K_(n-1) one color; at each new color join two copies, making that color bipartite and preserving old-color components. Gives 2^(k-1)(n-1) vertices without monochromatic odd C_n. Exact upper bound for every k>=2,odd n>3 is unpaid; a sufficiently-large-n theorem would not alone match.

334127.title: The forbidden-minor embedding conjecture for graph metrics
334127.statement: Let $L$ be a finite set of graphs. A graph **excludes** $L$ as a minor if it contains no member of $L$ as a minor, where minors are obtained by edge contractions, edge deletions, and vertex deletions. **Forbidden-minor embedding conjecture.** There exists a constant $C_L<\infty$ such that every metric on any graph excluding $L$ as a minor can be embedded into $\ell_1$ with distortion at most $C_L$. This conjecture generalizes the Planar Conjecture and remains open despite substantial work on low-distortion embeddings of graph metrics.
334127.exact_gap_or_derivation: Literal says every metric on a graph, while usual graph-metric conjectures use shortest-path lengths; arbitrary metric interpretation is stronger. Empty forbidden set also needs convention. No metric-embedding body or full uniform distortion proof; no domain correction credited.

329885.title: The Reed–Wood conjecture on minors of 2-regular graphs
329885.statement:
Let $t$ be a positive integer. A **$2$-regular graph** is a graph in which every vertex has degree $2$; such a graph is a disjoint union of cycles.

**Reed–Wood conjecture.** Every graph with average degree at least

$$
\tfrac{4}{3}t-2
$$

contains every $2$-regular $t$-vertex graph as a minor.

This conjecture extends the paper's theorem for $k$ disjoint cycles of the same order by allowing the cycles in the desired minor to have different orders. It was stated by Reed and Wood and remains open here.
329885.exact_gap_or_derivation: Need disjoint branch-set models for every prescribed cycle length partition of t at average degree4t/3-2. Equal-length packing does not imply mixed-length packing; deleting a long cycle can destroy the residual degree bound. Same-source historical notes329886-329889 do not dispose of this ID.

381243.title: The vertex bound conjecture for critical graphs of tree-depth k
381243.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of tree-depth $k$, meaning that $k$ is the least number of labels in a vertex ranking of $G$ such that every path joining two vertices with the same label contains a vertex with a higher label. A graph is **critical** if it has tree-depth $k$ and every proper minor has smaller tree-depth. **Vertex bound conjecture.** Every critical graph with tree-depth $k$ has at most

$$
2^{k-1}
$$

vertices. This conjecture concerns the possible size of minor-minimal obstructions at each tree-depth; the supplied source does not state whether the bound has been proved or disproved.
381243.exact_gap_or_derivation: Critical graph must be connected: if two components, tree-depth is the maximum of component depths and deleting a nonmaximal component preserves depth. A depth-k rooted forest can nevertheless have arbitrarily many branches. Need criticality to bound total branch sizes by2^(k-1), not just height. No such full induction or counterexample.

327550.title: The shrub-depth characterization by vertex-minors
327550.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a class of graphs. A graph is of **bounded shrub-depth** if its shrub-depth is bounded by some fixed integer.

**Shrub-depth characterization conjecture.** The class $\mathcal{C}$ is of bounded shrub-depth if, and only if, there exists an integer $t$ such that no graph $G\in\mathcal{C}$ contains a path of length $t$ as a vertex-minor.

This asks whether excluding a fixed path as a vertex-minor exactly characterizes classes of graphs of bounded shrub-depth. The surrounding discussion presents it as a natural question following the construction of cographs containing arbitrarily long paths as pivot-minors; its resolution is not specified in the source.
327550.exact_gap_or_derivation: Excluding a path as an induced subgraph is insufficient; local complementations can create new paths. Need both uniform shrub-depth bound from vertex-minor exclusion and converse under exact path-length convention. Source mention of pivot-minors cannot be silently substituted.

381233.title: Characterization of strongly Tutte-descriptive activities
381233.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $\psi$ be an activity. The activity $\psi$ is **strongly Tutte-descriptive** if it is Tutte-descriptive and induces a partition

$$
2^{E(G)}=\biguplus_{T\text{ spanning tree of }G}[T\backslash \psi(T),T\cup \psi(T)].
$$

**Characterization of strongly Tutte-descriptive activities.** For any graph $G$, an activity $\psi$ is strongly Tutte-descriptive if and only if there exists a decision tree $\Delta$ such that $\psi$ equals the $\Delta$-activity.

The conjecture seeks to characterize precisely the activities arising from decision trees among those inducing the stated partition of the subgraphs. The right-to-left implication has already been proved in the paper through Theorem and Theorem; the converse is therefore the unresolved direction in the source.

325802.title: Erdős–Faudree–Gould–Gyárfás–Rousseau–Schelp 2/3 conjecture
325802.statement: Let $G$ be a complete graph whose edges are coloured with three colours. This conjecture asks for the sharp bound suggested by Kierstead's three-colouring construction, which shows that a small set cannot be guaranteed to monochromatically dominate significantly more than $2/3$ of the vertices. The supplied source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

325866.title: Erdős–Gould–Yuster–Oz conjecture on dense chordal subgraphs
325866.statement:
A chordal subgraph of a graph is a subgraph with no induced cycle of length greater than three.

**Erdős–Gould–Yuster–Oz conjecture.** Any graph with $n$ vertices and more than $n^2/3$ edges contains a chordal subgraph with at least $8n/3-4$ edges. The complete tripartite graph with one additional edge shows that this would be sharp.

The conjecture seeks the sharp lower bound for a large chordal subgraph above the density threshold $n^2/3$. The source records only a weaker bound of $7n/3-6$ edges, so the conjecture is unresolved there.

326561.title: The treewidth formula for Kneser graphs
326561.statement:
Let $G$ be the Kneser graph whose vertices are the $k$-element subsets of an $n$-element set, with two vertices adjacent when the corresponding subsets are disjoint.

**Treewidth conjecture.** If $n \geq 3k$ and $k \geq 2$, then

$$
\operatorname{tw}(G)=\binom{n-1}{k}-1.
$$

The paper proves this formula for the values of $n$ covered by its main theorem and conjectures that it also holds for smaller values of $n$. The conjecture concerns the exact treewidth of Kneser graphs beyond the established range.

324594.title: Connected tree-width duality conjecture
324594.statement: Let $G$ be a graph. A **bramble** in $G$ is a set of pairwise touching connected subsets of $V(G)$, where two subsets touch if they have a vertex in common or $G$ contains an edge between them. The **connected order** of a bramble is the least order of a cover spanning a connected subgraph, where the order is the least number of vertices needed to cover the bramble. Let $k\geq 0$ be an integer. **Connected tree-width duality conjecture.** A graph has connected tree-width at least $k$ if and only if it contains a bramble of connected order greater than $k$. This conjecture proposes the converse of the known fact that graphs of connected tree-width less than $k$ cannot have brambles of connected order greater than $k$; whether the converse holds is left open in the source.
324594.exact_gap_or_derivation: Standard tree-decomposition subtrees for touching bramble sets give a common bag by tree Helly, so a connected bag hits each bramble when such bags are supplied. Converse requires constructing a decomposition with connected bags from bounded connected bramble order; ordinary bramble duality controls bag size only. Exact connected-treewidth definition/source proof unread.

324630.title: The weighted expanding formulation of Seymour's conjecture
324630.statement: Let $D$ be a digraph without loops or two-cycles. Give each vertex a nonnegative real weight, and call a vertex **weakly expanding** when the weight of its second out-neighborhood is at least the weight of its first out-neighborhood. **Weighted expanding formulation of Seymour's conjecture.** Every digraph without loops or two-cycles has a vertex-weighting such that every vertex is weakly expanding. By the preceding argument, this formulation is equivalent to Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture. The paper uses it to relate the conjecture to an alternative involving strongly contracting vertices in the reverse digraph; it does not resolve the general case.
324630.exact_gap_or_derivation: All-zero nonnegative weights satisfy every inequality identically. Claimed equivalence to Seymour not proved and likely missing a nonzero convention. Source/references contradiction unresolved; wording correction zero.

336805.title: Ossona de Mendez–Oum–Wood defective colouring conjecture
336805.statement:
For a graph class $\mathcal{G}$, let $\chi_{\Delta}(\mathcal{G})$ be the minimum integer $k$ such that, for some integer $d$, every graph in $\mathcal{G}$ is $k$-colourable with defect $d$. For a graph $H$, let $\mathcal{M}_H$ be the class of $H$-minor-free graphs, and let $\operatorname{\overline{td}}(H)$ denote the connected tree-depth of $H$. **Ossona de Mendez–Oum–Wood's conjecture.** For every graph $H$, 
$$
\chi_{\Delta}(\mathcal{M}_H)=\operatorname{\overline{td}}(H)-1.
$$
 The conjecture is a defective-colouring analogue of Hadwiger's conjecture. The lower bound is proved, and the upper bound is known when $\operatorname{\overline{td}}(H)\leqslant 3$, when $H$ is complete bipartite, and when $H=K_t$; the general upper bound remains open.
336805.exact_gap_or_derivation: Defective coloring needs one d independent of graph order for each excluded H. Coloring bounded-size graphs separately or obtaining defect depending on order is insufficient. Need exact connected-tree-depth definition and full universal upper bound; no stronger current theorem body inspected.

353585.title: Bannister–Ojakian's shallow topological-minor conjecture for stack-number
353585.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, and let $k\geqslant 0$ be a half-integer. A graph $H$ is a **$k$-shallow topological minor** of $G$ if a subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to a subdivision of $H$ in which each edge is replaced by a path with at most $2k$ internal vertices. Write $\operatorname{sn}(G)$ for the stack-number of $G$. **Bannister–Ojakian's conjecture.** There exists a function $f$ such that for every graph $G$ and half-integer $k\geqslant 0$, if $H$ is any $k$-shallow topological minor of $G$, then

$$
\operatorname{sn}(H)\leqslant f(\operatorname{sn}(G),k).
$$

The conjecture proposed that stack-number is well-behaved under shallow topological minors. It was disproved by Dujmović, Eppstein, Hickingbotham, Morin, and Wood (2021).

356537.title: The cograph formulation of the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture
356537.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph. A **cograph** is either a single-vertex graph or a graph obtained by taking the vertex-disjoint union of two smaller cographs whose vertex sets form a pure pair. A graph $G$ is **$H$-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$.

**Cograph formulation of the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture.** For every graph $H$, there exists an $\varepsilon>0$ such that every $n$-vertex $H$-free graph $G$ contains an induced cograph of order $n^{\varepsilon}$.

Because cographs are perfect, this formulation is equivalent to the original Erdős–Hajnal conjecture. It is presented as a convenient reformulation for the paper's proof, while the conjecture remains open.
356537.exact_gap_or_derivation: An induced cograph of order m has clique or independent set >=sqrt(m): inductively color/cover perfect cograph, or recurse on joins/unions. Conversely an EH clique/independent set is a cograph. Thus a full polynomial cograph bound demands the full EH mechanism, not mere reformulation. Literal exact order n^epsilon also has rounding convention. No universal mechanism.

373605.title: Przybyło–Woźniak total 1-2 Conjecture
373605.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A total coloring is a function $g:V\cup E\to\{1,2,\dots,k\}$, with total vertex weight $\sigma^t(v)=g(v)+\sum_{v\in e}g(e)$. Adjacent vertices are distinguished when their total weights differ, and $\chi^t_{\Sigma}(G)$ is the least $k$ for which every adjacent pair is distinguished. **Total 1-2 Conjecture.** For every graph $G$, 
$$
\chi^t_{\Sigma}(G)\leq 2.
$$
 The supplied text gives no resolution of this total neighbor-sum-distinguishing conjecture, so it remains open.
373605.exact_gap_or_derivation: ORDINARY-ROUTES exact Boolean clauses, bipartite and all-cycle proofs, plus multilinear polynomial route. Missing global feasible edge labeling/nonzero reduced coefficient proof. No general result or current proof-body comparison.

324056.title: The planar-or-bounded-high-degree structure conjecture for graphs without a topological K_5
324056.statement:
Let $K_5$ denote the complete graph on five vertices. A graph is a **clique-sum** of graphs $G_1,\ldots,G_n$ if it is obtained by repeatedly gluing graphs along cliques. The **degree** of a vertex is its number of incident edges.

**Planar-or-bounded-high-degree conjecture.** There exist constants $D$ and $a$ such that every graph $G$ that does not contain $K_5$ as a topological minor can be expressed as a clique-sum of graphs $G_1,\ldots,G_n$ such that, for each $1\leq i\leq n$, either $G_i$ is planar or $G_i$ contains at most $a$ vertices of degree at least $D$.

This conjecture would strengthen the preceding structure theorem by removing the vortices and apex vertices from its planar alternative. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source context.
324056.exact_gap_or_derivation: Need universal D,a and actual clique-sum decomposition for every topological-K5-free graph, without vortices/apices. High-degree vertices in different summands cannot simply be bounded globally; splitting at arbitrary separators is not a clique-sum. No full structure theorem or obstruction.

353904.title: Deletable-subgraph size conjecture for minor-free graphs
353904.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, let $X\subseteq V(G)$, and let an $r$-deletable subgraph mean an induced subgraph that is colourable from every list assignment whose list sizes satisfy the degree-deficit condition in the source. Let $v(G)$ denote the number of vertices of $G$. **Deletable-subgraph size conjecture.** There exists a constant $k$ such that, for every $t$, there is a constant $c_t$ depending on $t$ such that if $G$ is $K_t$-minor-free, $X\subseteq V(G)$, and $G$ has no $kt$-deletable subgraph disjoint from $X$, then $v(G)\leq c_t|X|$. The conjecture would provide a strong structural bound for critical graphs used in precolouring-extension arguments; its resolution is not given in the source.
353904.exact_gap_or_derivation: Literal defers degree-deficit list condition to source. No exact r-deletable predicate can be recovered from this alone. X=empty would require some kt-deletable induced subgraph in every nonempty excluded-minor graph. Degeneracy bounds alone do not prove the needed deficit-list extension. All-t absolute k unpaid.
